claim: The AIRE gene promotes thymic presentation of tissue-specific molecules.
source: The AIRE gene plays a key role in the development of central immune tolerance by promoting thymic presentation of tissue-specific molecules.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a known function of AIRE.

claim: Patients with AIRE-deficiency develop multiple autoimmune manifestations.
source: Patients with AIRE-deficiency develop multiple autoimmune manifestations and display autoantibodies against the affected tissues.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and is supported by established knowledge about APS1/APECED.

claim: Patients with AIRE-deficiency display autoantibodies against the affected tissues.
source: Patients with AIRE-deficiency develop multiple autoimmune manifestations and display autoantibodies against the affected tissues.

claim: Meyer et al. (2016) reported that the spectrum of autoantibodies in patients with AIRE-deficiency is much broader than previously appreciated.
source: In 2016 it was reported that: i) the spectrum of autoantibodies in patients with AIRE-deficiency is much broader than previously appreciated; ii) neutralizing autoantibodies to type I interferons (IFNs) could provide protection against type 1 diabetes in these patients (Meyer et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a citation to a claim made by Meyer et al. (2016).

claim: Meyer et al. (2016) reported that neutralizing autoantibodies to type I interferons could provide protection against type 1 diabetes in AIRE-deficient patients.
source: In 2016 it was reported that: i) the spectrum of autoantibodies in patients with AIRE-deficiency is much broader than previously appreciated; ii) neutralizing autoantibodies to type I interferons (IFNs) could provide protection against type 1 diabetes in these patients (Meyer et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a citation to a claim made by Meyer et al. (2016).

claim: The authors found no evidence for a broad autoantibody spectrum in AIRE-deficient patients when using an independent patient cohort and similar experimental approach.
source: We attempted to replicate these new findings using a similar experimental approach in an independent patient cohort, and found no evidence for either conclusion.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the abstract, based on the authors' reanalysis.

claim: The authors found no evidence for an association between neutralizing autoantibodies to type I interferons and protection against type 1 diabetes in AIRE-deficient patients.
source: We attempted to replicate these new findings using a similar experimental approach in an independent patient cohort, and found no evidence for either conclusion.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the abstract, based on the authors' experimental data.

claim: AIRE encodes a transcription factor that promotes thymic presentation of genes with limited peripheral tissue distribution.

claim: AIRE-mediated antigen presentation is critical for the negative selection of autoreactive T-cells.
source: AIRE-mediated antigen exposes naïve T-cells to self-molecules that otherwise would not be present in the thymus, and is therefore critical for the negative selection of autoreactive T-cells.
